title: The Silent Salt
premise: Freya Almeida has spent nine years hiding in the Salt Valley, the one place in the realm where magic cannot cross, exiled after her storm-calling killed a village elder. When the crown's witch-hunters breach the valley's edge and begin dragging out those with dormant gifts, Freya learns the valley's silence was never natural—it was forged by a covenant between realms that someone at court is deliberately breaking to harvest magic for the throne. To survive, she must leave the only home she's known, gather the scattered oath-keepers of three realms, and reforge the broken covenant before the thirteenth moon turns. In the end, Freya discovers the covenant demands a memory as payment: she sacrifices her recollection of the valley and everyone in it, sealing the realms apart but free—and walks into a world where belonging must be built anew rather than remembered.
about_author: Ines Vane is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping coastlines that no longer exist on modern charts. She writes fantasy about places that remember more than people do.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Nine years of quiet life in Salt Valley, tending salt-pans and hiding her dead gift, until a hunter's arrow lands at her feet bearing the crown's sigil. The emotional beat is the fragile comfort of routine cracking open—she realizes invisibility was always borrowed time.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Witch-hunters burn the eastern farms; her neighbor Tam, whose gift never woke, is taken anyway. Freya uses a flicker of storm-magic to save his daughter, feeling the valley's silence push back against her like a held breath. Beat: guilt resurfacing—the first time power has felt like mercy instead of murder.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. An old oath-keeper, Maren, reveals the valley's magic-deadness is a covenant seal, not geography—and it is failing. Each lunar turn weakens it; the thirteenth moon will shatter it entirely. Beat: dread reframed as purpose; Freya's exile suddenly has a shape and a deadline.

chapters.title: What the Crown Wants
chapters.summary: POV shift to Corvus Hale, the crown's chief hunter, who knows exactly what he serves: the king is draining captured gifts to feed something beneath the palace. Corvus tells himself the culling prevents catastrophe. Beat: chilling competence—he is not cruel, which makes him worse.

chapters.title: Leaving
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She crosses the valley's boundary for the first time, and her magic floods back painfully—every suppressed storm returning at once. Maren gives her a shattered oath-stone, one third of the covenant key. Beat: terror and exhilaration entwined; leaving means becoming what they hunt.

chapters.title: The Drowned Choir
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In the flooded city of Vess, she finds the second oath-keeper: Sable, a tide-speaker who lost her voice to the crown's drainings and speaks through water. Beat: grief made visible; Freya sees her own possible future in Sable's silence.

chapters.title: A Hunt in Earnest
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. He tracks the storm-signature from Vess and recognizes its pattern—it matches records from the massacre nine years ago. He begins hunting not a rumor but a name. Beat: the net tightening; the past is a scent trail.

chapters.title: The Memory Market
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In the bazaar-city of Ondu, memories are currency. To buy passage, Freya sells a single day—one she chooses badly, losing the last afternoon with her mother. Beat: the theme of memory made literal and costly; some prices are only understood afterward.

chapters.title: Third Stone, Third Keeper
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The final oath-keeper is a mountain-wright named Ivo, imprisoned in Ondu for refusing to sell his gift. Freya breaks him out using a storm small enough to pass unnoticed—but not small enough to hide from Corvus. Beat: first true act of rebellion; no way back now.

chapters.title: The King Beneath
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. He descends into the vaults beneath the palace and finally sees what he feeds: a bound ancient thing, half-starved, whispering promises. Corvus wavers for the first time. Beat: the corruption of power shown from inside; doubt planted like a seed.

chapters.title: Campfire Confessions
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The three keepers shelter in the high passes; Freya confesses the truth of the massacre—that the elder she killed was trying to sacrifice a child to feed the same thing under the palace. Beat: shame transmuted into resolve; her crime was a warning she failed to hear.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Pass
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Offered amnesty for his family, Ivo sells their route to Corvus—then watches the hunters take his family anyway. Beat: power corrupting the desperate; betrayal that buys nothing.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Passes
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Ambushed, Freya unleashes a full storm for the first time since exile—magnificent and horrifying. They escape, but Sable is gravely wounded shielding her. Beat: power's seduction and cost in a single breath; Freya fears what she is becoming.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. At court, Corvus witnesses the king feed a captured child's gift to the thing below and understands there was never any protection in service. He burns his commission. Beat: the turn of the antagonist; the hunter becomes a deserter.

chapters.title: Sable's Bargain
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Dying, Sable offers her remaining tide-gift to complete the stones, asking only that Freya carry her memory of the drowned choir into the new covenant. Beat: love as legacy; grief given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: The Road to the Rift
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, joined by a shadowing Corvus who offers intelligence on the palace wards. Distrust simmers, but his knowledge is real. Beat: uneasy alliance; enemies discovering shared ground without yet sharing trust.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn Rising
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. The moon nears full; the rift above the palace yawns wider, and the drained gifts of hundreds hang in the air like trapped weather. Corvus leads them through the ward-labyrinth he helped design. Beat: countdown pressure; every step forward is a step into the trap's heart.

chapters.title: The Vault of Stolen Sky
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In the vaults, the bound entity offers Freya everything: her valley restored, her crime undone, her mother's sold day returned—in exchange for letting the covenant die. Beat: the climax of temptation; belonging offered as a lie.

chapters.title: Reforge
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. With Ivo's stone, Sable's tide-gift, and her own storm-heart, Freya reforges the covenant at the moment the thirteenth moon crests. The entity fights her with her own worst memory—the killing—until she accepts it fully rather than fleeing it. Beat: climax; power redeemed by ownership, not denial.

chapters.title: The Price of Seals
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The covenant completes and demands its payment: a memory of equal weight to the binding. Freya gives up the valley itself—its faces, its salt wind, nine years of quiet. Beat: bittersweet triumph; victory measured in what is willingly surrendered.

chapters.title: After the Storm
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The hunts end; the freed gifts settle across the land like rain. Corvus turns himself over to a reformed council; Ivo rebuilds. Freya stands outside the valley she can no longer remember, holding an oath-stone warm in her palm. Beat: the world exhales; wounds acknowledged, not erased.

chapters.title: A Door Left Open
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A girl from the valley finds her—a stranger now, though the girl calls her by name. Freya doesn't remember her, but chooses to walk beside her anyway. Beat: resolution of the theme; belonging rebuilt not from memory but from choice, one step at a time.
